title: [Chapitre] VII. Analysis situs (troisième mouture) : notes manuscrites (23-26/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: an abstract axiomatics for 'ateliers' (workshops), meaning categories or sets of tame (here polyhedral) 'figures'. The data are a set M of figures with two relations. X ≤ Y is the structural or face relation; it is strict when X < Y. X ≪ Y is the 'is contained in' relation, read geometrically as the figure X lying in the figure Y. L ⊂ M is the set of ≪-minimal elements, the points. The previous page set the goal: describe polyhedral special ateliers satisfying L1–L3 and AtCL(spec) in terms of (M, ≤, ≪, ∦). There the transversality relation ∦ on M is to be recovered from a graph relation ∥ on the points (p.24, (3)). This page isolates the conditions that involve only ≤ and ≪, independently of ∥.

The axioms are as follows.
- (ML0): X ≤ Y ⇒ X ≪ Y.
- (ML1): if X', X'' ≤ X and x ∈ L with x ≪ X' and x ≪ X'', then there is Z with x ≪ Z and Z ≤ X', X''. That is, the 'intersection figure' X'∩X'' acts as an infimum for ≪, at least on points. A marginal note says this should eventually be replaced by properties of the Inf of X', X'', without requiring a common upper bound X.

Definitions:
- omb(X) = {x ∈ L | x ≪ X}: the 'shadow', or underlying point set, of X.
- omb(X)° = omb(X) \ ⋃_{Y<X} omb(Y): the points not lying in any proper subfigure, i.e. the 'open cell'.
- x ≪° X iff x ≪ X and (x ≪ X' ≤ X ⇒ X' = X). Likewise Y ≪° X iff X is minimal in {X' ≤ X | Y ≪ X'}.

The new axiom (ML2) says omb(X)° ≠ ∅. Lemma 1 asserts the equivalence of five conditions:
- (i) X ≤ Y;
- (ii) X ≪ Y;
- (ii bis) omb X ⊂ omb Y;
- (iii) omb(X)° ⊂ omb(Y);
- (iv) omb(X)° ∩ omb(Y) ≠ ∅.

The forward implications run as follows. (i)⇒(ii) is ML0. (ii)⇒(ii bis) holds by transitivity of ≪. (ii bis)⇒(iii) is trivial. (iii)⇒(iv) needs ML2.

The key step is (iv)⇒(i). Take x ∈ omb(X)° ∩ omb(Y). ML1 gives Z ≤ X, Y with x ≪ Z. Minimality (x ≪° X) forces Z = X, hence X ≤ Y.

In modern terms, Lemma 1 is the statement that, in a cell or stratified decomposition, the face relation coincides with inclusion of closed cells. It is also the frontier condition: if an open cell meets a closed cell, it lies in it. The next page adds two consequences. First, distinct open cells are disjoint. Second, (ML3): the open cells of the faces of X partition omb(X). Together these make L, M a regular-cell-complex-like structure determined by its points.
errors: In the proof of (iv)⇒(i), ML1 is applied to X and Y, but ML1 as stated requires X', X'' ≤ X for some common X. For arbitrary X, Y no such common upper bound is given. Grothendieck visibly hesitates: he strikes out the 'X, Y' after 'Z ≤', and the marginal note proposes replacing the hypothesis by Inf properties. The lemma therefore needs the strengthened, Inf-type version of ML1 (no common upper bound).
(ii)⇒(ii bis) tacitly uses transitivity of ≪ (x ≪ X ≪ Y ⇒ x ≪ Y), which is not listed among the ML axioms on this page.

ideas.what: Axiomatizing a polyhedral/tame 'atelier' by a set of figures with a face order ≤, a containment relation ≪, and points defined as ≪-minimal elements
ideas.modern_name: Face poset of a regular cell complex / stratified space; abstract tame topology
ideas.usually_credited_to: Regular CW complexes and face posets (Björner and others, 1980s); tame topology programme (Grothendieck, Esquisse 1984; o-minimality: van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorn)
ideas.where_published: Only the general tame-topology programme appears, in Esquisse d'un programme §5; this axiomatics does not

ideas.what: omb(X) (points of X) and omb(X)° (points not in any proper face), i.e. closed and open cells
ideas.modern_name: Closed cell / open cell (relative interior) of a stratum

ideas.what: Lemma 1: face relation ⇔ containment ⇔ inclusion of point sets ⇔ open cell meets closed cell
ideas.modern_name: Frontier condition for stratifications / cell decompositions
ideas.usually_credited_to: Whitney, Thom, Mather (stratification theory); standard for regular cell complexes

missed.claim: A purely combinatorial characterization of polyhedral special ateliers by (M, ≤, ≪) plus a graph relation ∥ on the points, with axioms ML0–ML3. This is an intrinsic, point-based axiomatics of tame figures, distinct from o-minimal structures. It was left incomplete: ML1 still needs reformulation as an Inf property.
missed.quote: Il faudra remplacer, avec X'≤X, X''≤X, par les propriétés des Inf (« X', X'' »)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It suggests a poset-theoretic route to tame topology, comparable to face-poset or cellular-stratified-space axiomatics. Specialists might compare it with o-minimal cell decomposition and with exit-path or poset-stratified approaches.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics on the page is routine: open versus closed cells and the frontier condition. What is mildly interesting is that it belongs to Grothendieck's unpublished intrinsic axiomatics of tame/polyhedral 'ateliers'. That framework is only sketched programmatically in the Esquisse.
transcription_corrections: Left marginal note beside Lemma 1 seems to read '(ML 2) avant le Lemme 1' rather than '(ML 2) énoncé du lemme 1'.

The ML1 margin note reads roughly 'Il faudra [?] remplacer, avec X'≤X, X''≤X, par les propriétés des Inf (« X', X'' »)'. The crossed-out version at line 4 suggests the second condition was 'X''≤X', not 'X''≪X'.
In the proof of (iv)⇒(i), 'Z ≤ X, Y' has X and Y struck through, then rewritten. The final line reads 'x ≪ Z ≤ X, d'où Z = X puisque x ≪° X, donc X ≤ Y, qed.'
Under (ML1): 'alors ∃ Z ∈ M avec x ≪ Z et Z ≤ X', X''' (the 'M' is missing in the transcription).
